title: Applying for and varying an AFS licence
subject: This guide provides detailed guidance for applicants on how to apply for an Australian financial services (AFS) licence or to vary an existing licence. It covers the application process, documentation requirements, and ASIC's assessment criteria.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth), which requires persons carrying on a financial services business to hold an AFS licence. It is intended for individuals and entities seeking to obtain or vary an AFS licence, and explains ASIC's role in assessing applications and the legislative framework governing licensing.
ruling: ASIC states that it will assess AFS licence applications against the statutory criteria in the Corporations Act, including whether the applicant is of good fame and character, has adequate financial resources, and has appropriate organisational competence. The guide outlines ASIC's approach to evaluating these criteria, including the requirement for applicants to demonstrate they can comply with their general obligations under s 912A. ASIC provides practical guidance on the information and documentation that must be submitted, and explains that it may impose licence conditions or refuse applications where criteria are not met. The guide also addresses variations to existing licences, including notification requirements and assessment processes.
